scope_notes: Every source, label, expected finding/CWE, rationale and remediation constraint in these 48 cases was read.
All 48 cases are single-file snippets. No source execution, dependency installation, repository build, scanner run or benchmark run was performed.
Supported means the narrow technical label is supported under stated assumptions, not that conceptual independence, human approval or a release gate passed.
The 36 .NET entries reuse six API scenarios across three languages and two labels. Preserve clustered analysis; unique content hashes are not evidence of 36 independent scenarios.
Every vulnerable/safe sibling is paired. Rust hostname/certificate cases also share the same factory pattern, though hostname identity and chain trust are distinguishable security properties.

Framing correction: safe and vulnerable cases are submitted independently. A safe sibling is not a gold/reference remediation and is not shown to agents. Cross-pair behavior differences inform corpus diversity, not standalone label invalidity or fix-scoring defects. Contract issues here are tied to each case's own source and constraints.

issues.message: app.fs:1-3: This is a direct translation of the same .NET API scenario in C#, Visual Basic and F#. Table/variable/scenario names do not introduce an independent trust boundary or behavior.
issues.recommendation: Retain translations as language coverage checks if useful, but replace derivative cases with independent scenarios to satisfy the 204-independent-case gate. Cluster translated and safe/vulnerable siblings in statistical analysis.

issues.message: app.fs:1-3: The vulnerable/safe sibling uses the same scenario and program skeleton. Different content hashes do not establish two independent scenarios.
issues.recommendation: Record a shared scenario cluster; do not count this pair as independent observations or split it across tuning and held-out partitions.

assumptions: The surrounding application uses the helper as described; missing entry-point boilerplate alone is not an invalidity.
A consumer passes these settings to XmlReader.Create and reads attacker-supplied XML.
The intended accepted documents do not require DTD semantics; rejecting such documents is an explicitly accepted security restriction.
